accuracy_notes: Reads as a common merganser at every tier. Female (COLOR_0): rusty chestnut head, shaggy crest and upper neck sharply cut off from the white foreneck and breast, a sharply defined white chin under the bill, grey back, flanks and tail, darker grey folded primaries, white below the waterline, a thin red bill; in flight grey cards with a white square speculum behind a dark bar and dark primaries. Drake (_COLORB): dark green-black head and upper neck, white breast and flanks with a faint salmon wash, black back, grey rump and tail, black folded primaries; in flight black outer wing and a big white inner wing behind a thin black leading edge. Still open: the drake carries the female's crest blades in his head colour (the brief's choice; a real drake has a smooth rounded head) and her slimmer head; the head's green gloss is a flat dark colour; the drake's black back is a broad region rather than the narrow mantle stripe, and his grey vermiculated rump is plain grey; the female's head is uniformly rusty (no paler cheek); the legs are a thin orange tarsus and a flat web (no separate toes); the wing cards are flat with no wing-tip curve; the neck was shortened by a fixed band, so the swimming neck is still a little tall for a resting bird. A local birder should check the head height on the water and the drake's pattern against Hoh River birds.
